title: Immutable host-native local modules
summary: Relocatable macOS/Windows modules preserve source and dependency identity through verified inventories and atomic installation.

dates.note: Exact project start/end dates remain unknown. Direct local source/history review on 2026-10-29 supplements the supplied October 5 snapshot and separately dated owner statements. Commit milestones and review dates are not project starts or release dates.

facts.text: Built host-native macOS and Windows module builders using disposable source copies, recording source provenance and including applicable dirty/untracked content.
Implemented canonical payload inventories, lock/wheelhouse fingerprints, read-only permissions, archive round-trip verification and atomic installation under unique labels.
Detected runtime references back into source checkouts and refused overwriting existing module identities.
The local-module suites contain 78 Python test definitions in the supplied snapshot; this is not a count of executed or passing tests.

Separated lightweight MCP-runtime and full desktop-application package profiles, rejecting cross-host production builds and checking the product-owned asset/script contract before starting expensive packaging.

notes: Host-native local rehearsal is distinct from RHEL compatibility, Depot/Lmod publication, LSF execution and cluster-provider acceptance.

Read-only permissions, inventories and no-overwrite identities are integrity controls, not proof of bit-for-bit reproducible builds across machines. Builds include external interpreters/toolchains whose identities and compatibility remain part of the recorded context.
